question.knowledge_point: Finding the Final Position of a Particle Given a Velocity-Time Graph
question.problem:
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/14042727/assets/6c0f74fa4820cd8e6945666ab90e0eafac4cc1ada7578fb5a053f197adf08084.png)

The graph above shows the velocity of an object moving in a straight line along the $x$-axis. At time $t=1$ the particle is located at the position $x=2.$ What is the position of the particle at time $t=7?$
question.worked_solution:
The position of the particle at $t=7$ is equal to its position at $t=1$ plus the total displacement over $t\in [1,7].$ Therefore, we can calculate it as follows:

$$
x(7)=x(1)+{\int }_{1}^{7}v(t)\,\text{d}t
$$

We are told that $x(1)=2$, and we can compute the integral ${\int }_{1}^{7}v(t)\,\text{d}t$ by finding the signed area under the graph from $t=1$ to $t=7.$ Computing the signed area, we get

$$
{\int }_{1}^{7}v(t)\,\text{d}t=0.
$$

Therefore,

$$
x(7)=2+0=2
$$

So the position of the particle at $t=7$ is $x=2.$
